title: Before AI - Nvidia's greatest technical achievements (and bombs)
gist: A SemiWiki forum opinion post ranks Nvidia's pre-AI technical milestones—Riva 128 (1997), GeForce 2 Go, nForce, CUDA (2007) and Maxwell (2014)—arguing CUDA is the foundation of Nvidia's current success and Maxwell opened an efficiency lead AMD never closed, alongside missteps like the FX 'Dust Buster', the GTX 970 lawsuit and the RTX 4080 12GB unlaunch.

insights.claim: The 1997 Nvidia Riva 128 chipset offered gamers 24-bit color when 3DFx Voodoo was often limited to 16-bit in 3D, and per the forum author it saved Nvidia from bankruptcy.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Historical context: Nvidia's survival hinged on a single product win, illustrating winner-take-most GPU dynamics.
insights.quote: This chip saved the company from bankruptcy.

insights.claim: CUDA, launched in 2007 and initially used by only a few high-end 3D software products, delivered a huge performance leap over CPUs for specialized tasks and is, in the forum author's view, the foundation of all of Nvidia's success today.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Reinforces the software-ecosystem moat thesis for NVDA: the AI franchise rests on a 2007 platform bet.
insights.quote: CUDA is the foundation for all of Nvidia's success today, imo.

insights.claim: Nvidia's 2014 Maxwell (900 series) GPUs nearly doubled power efficiency over the prior generation without a manufacturing process change, and the author claims AMD has never caught up in efficiency since.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Architectural efficiency gains independent of process nodes underpin Nvidia's durable perf/watt edge versus AMD.
insights.quote: AMD has never caught up in efficiency since this uplift.

insights.claim: The GeForce 8000 series was Nvidia's first lineup spanning very low end to very high end with strong price/performance, putting AMD/ATi on the back foot.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Full-stack product coverage has historically been how Nvidia pressured AMD share.

insights.claim: The forum author disputes that the Nvidia GeForce was the first GPU, citing earlier GPUs such as the ANTIC chip on the 1979 Atari 800, and notes ray tracing (RTX) is only now gaining traction after being 'around the corner' for decades.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Marketing firsts aside, ray tracing adoption is a slow-burn feature rather than a demand driver.

insights.claim: Around 2003 Nvidia's FX series stumbled: the top FX5800 was nicknamed 'The Dust Buster' for its loud cooling and higher-than-expected power draw, while the FX 5200 was no faster than older GeForce cards.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Even dominant GPU vendors have had product-cycle misfires; execution risk is real.

insights.claim: Nvidia paid every GeForce GTX 970 owner $30 after a lawsuit over the card being advertised as 4GB when 0.5GB of that memory was very slow.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Precedent for consumer-litigation exposure over memory specs.

insights.claim: Nvidia 'unlaunched' the GeForce RTX 4080 12GB after consumer pushback over poor naming.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Shows consumer-segment brand sensitivity that Nvidia will reverse course on.
